answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit tied to a unique hardware-rooted cipher key, and each epoch they must solve a rotating proof-of-work chained to that key. Duplicate identities share one key and thus one stake, so spinning up many sybils multiplies capital cost linearly while rewards stay capped per key. Like a quill signing a reef of ledger entries, every attestation is signed and slashable if equivocated, making forgery cost more than honest participation.
